a000.label: not_supported
a000.reason: The document establishes abundant Yellowstone cutthroat trout inside the park, but does not identify them as the primary fish species.

a001.label: supported
a001.reason: The documents describe mustangs as commonly called wild horses of the American west and establish populations in all six listed states.

a002.label: supported
a002.reason: The document explicitly places more than half of North America's mustangs in Nevada.

a003.label: supported
a003.reason: The document establishes BLM management through Herd Management Areas and continued protection of some free-roaming populations under the Act.

a004.label: supported
a004.reason: The document explicitly establishes abundant Yellowstone cutthroat trout in the river inside Yellowstone National Park.

a005.label: supported
a005.reason: The document explicitly lists browns, whitefish, rainbows, and cutthroat trout below Knowles Falls.

a006.label: not_supported
a006.reason: The document assigns the mix of large browns and rainbows to the stretch upstream of Mallard's Rest. The subsequent Paradise Valley section supports rainbow dominance and the presence of browns, but does not establish their large size there.
